shouldFix.title: The W edges gate later SATISFIED cycles on other rows' leftovers without saying whether they are scheduling order or additional eligibility criteria, and D-036's own condition-2 disclaimer is not carried forward
shouldFix.finding: D-036, the entry this succeeds, closes with 'Condition 2 follows SF-3; condition 4 follows D-001/D-002; this entry changes neither.' D-139 has no successor to that clause: measured, SF-3 occurs zero times and 'changes neither' zero times in the draft. Into that silence it adds wait edges that gate a row's SATISFIED cycle on other rows' leftovers. W1 makes a DR-131 SATISFIED cycle wait on leftover-design of DR-131, of DR-117 and of DR-101 all closing. D-056's five gates require none of DR-117's or DR-101's leftovers to close for DR-131 to be eligible; they test that row's own contract, remainder and gate mapping. So on one reading W1 is a scheduling preference about drafting order, which is squarely within a D-036 successor's authority, and on another it is an extra bar on DR-131 SATISFIED beyond D-056 — which would be a condition-2 change the predecessor expressly disclaimed making. The entry's own W3 shows it knows the distinction and draws it for a different row: a DR-133 SATISFIED cycle 'waits only on D-056's five gates holding for DR-133 at that later cycle'. Applying the gates-only formulation to DR-133 and a leftover-closure formulation to DR-131 and DR-117, with no statement of why the difference is ordering rather than criteria, is what leaves the ambiguity. The preserved general clauses do not resolve it either: the Explicitly-not-scheduled section says 'Scheduling authorizes drafting only', but W1 by its terms constrains a SATISFIED cycle rather than a drafting act, so the reader cannot tell whether that sentence reaches it.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: The lawful reading is available and is probably the intended one: the entry is titled sequencing, its decision type is 'Sequencing only', it disclaims admitting leftover-design to SATISFIED, and it preserves D-133's rule that leftover-design is not a splittable remainder. Nothing is decided wrongly; the criterion-versus-order status of two edges is simply not stated where a later cycle would need it.
shouldFix.repair: Carry D-036's disclaimer forward and label the edges. One clause in the W section: these edges order the drafting of later cycles and add no SATISFIED criteria; D-056's five gates, applied at that later cycle, remain the only eligibility test, and condition 2 continues to follow SF-3 — this entry changes neither condition 2 nor condition 4. If instead W1's DR-117 and DR-101 edges are meant to bind a DR-131 SATISFIED cycle even when D-056's gates hold, that is a condition-2 change and needs to be said in terms and justified, not left to inference from a sequencing entry.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Fifteen attacks run, one landed. Custody is intact and, unlike the D-138 cycle, clean at the control plane: the dispatch and the sole review prompt pin the subject at the same digest 40cda3c8, it held at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left 3c215ab, and file 08, COORD and file 12 sat at their pins with a clean tree. The entry is careful work. It is the act file 12 §7 item 4 names and that D-036's own successor rule requires; its three characterisations of D-036 reproduce verbatim from D-036's bytes; it schedules the three owed hygiene acts the D-133, D-136 and D-138 cycles produced rather than leaving them floating; and on the sharpest attack — inventing a leftover inventory — it holds completely: all eight named leftovers resolve to their cited recordings, and it expressly declines to characterise the rows it does not name, which is the honest handling of a subset. Nothing is marked SATISFIED, no Class A is opened, no register row is added, and the readiness effect of zero at 4 of 32 matches live file 08. What blocks is one unstated distinction. D-036 closes by disclaiming any change to conditions 2 and 4; D-139 carries no successor to that clause — SF-3 and 'changes neither' each occur zero times — and into that silence adds wait edges gating a row's SATISFIED cycle on other rows' leftovers. W1 makes a DR-131 SATISFIED cycle wait on DR-117's and DR-101's leftovers closing, which D-056's five gates do not require. Read as scheduling order that is plainly within a sequencing successor's authority; read as a bar it is a condition-2 change the predecessor disclaimed. The entry's own W3 draws exactly this distinction for DR-133 — 'waits only on D-056's five gates' — so it knows the difference and applies it to one row but not the others, and the preserved 'scheduling authorizes drafting only' sentence does not obviously reach an edge phrased as constraining a SATISFIED cycle. One clause carrying D-036's disclaimer forward and labelling the edges as order rather than criteria closes it, and everything else in the entry should carry into turn 2 unchanged.
